paper_a.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling (Lipman et al., 2022)

paper_b.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Rectified Flow (Liu, Gong, Liu, 2022)

metadata.description: Nearly simultaneous (within 1 month) independent discoveries of the same core idea: learn ODE-based generative models by regressing a neural velocity field onto the direction of straight-line interpolation between noise and data. The training objectives are mathematically identical. Flow Matching provides the broader theoretical framework (conditional flow matching for arbitrary paths, gradient equivalence theorem); Rectified Flow provides the rectification/reflow procedure for iteratively straightening trajectories and enabling few-step generation.

matches.explanation: Both define the same object: a continuous normalizing flow (CNF) defined by an ODE $dx/dt = v(x,t)$ that transports a source distribution (Gaussian) to a target distribution (data) over $t \in [0,1]$. Identical mathematical framework.

THE core shared contribution. Both independently arrive at the same training procedure: sample $x_0 \sim N(0,I)$, $x_1 \sim q$ (data), form $x_t = (1-t)x_0 + tx_1$, and minimize $\|v_\theta(x_t, t) - (x_1 - x_0)\|^2$. Flow Matching calls this OT-CFM (optimal transport conditional flow matching); Rectified Flow calls it the rectified flow objective. Mathematically identical loss functions.

Both condition on individual data points to make training tractable. Flow Matching frames this as 'conditional flow matching' with a general theoretical framework (arbitrary conditional paths, gradient equivalence theorem). Rectified Flow frames it directly as regression on the linear interpolation direction. Same practical operation; Flow Matching provides the more general theoretical lens.

The intractable 'flow matching' objective (before conditioning) is a theoretical construct in Flow Matching that motivates the CFM objective. Rectified Flow does not define this intermediate intractable objective, going directly to the tractable regression loss.

The gradient equivalence theorem ($\nabla_\theta L_{CFM} = \nabla_\theta L_{FM}$) is a key theoretical contribution of Flow Matching. It proves that the tractable conditional objective optimizes the same function as the intractable marginal objective. Rectified Flow does not state or prove this result, instead directly justifying the regression objective.

The rectification/reflow procedure (iteratively solving the ODE to create new couplings and retraining) is unique to Rectified Flow. This is a major contribution: it straightens trajectories and reduces transport cost, enabling few-step generation. Flow Matching does not have this iterative refinement.
Distillation of rectified flows into one-step generators is unique to Rectified Flow. Flow Matching does not address one-step generation.
Image-to-image transfer via rectified flow between arbitrary distribution pairs is a unique application of Rectified Flow. Flow Matching focuses on noise-to-data generation.
The monotonic transport cost reduction theorem for rectification is a theoretical contribution unique to Rectified Flow.

Both demonstrate that their approach achieves competitive generation quality with fewer sampling steps than diffusion models, thanks to straighter ODE trajectories. Flow Matching emphasizes the efficiency gain from OT paths; Rectified Flow quantifies straightness and achieves few-step/one-step generation via rectification + distillation.

unmatched_paper_a_explanations.DP_FM.2: Intractable flow matching objective. Theoretical construct motivating CFM; not present in Rectified Flow.
unmatched_paper_a_explanations.TP_FM.1: Gradient equivalence theorem proving CFM = FM in gradient. Key theoretical result not in Rectified Flow.

unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_RF.3: Rectification/reflow for iteratively straightening trajectories. Major unique contribution.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.DP_RF.4: Distillation for one-step generation. Not in Flow Matching.
unmatched_paper_b_explanations.TP_RF.1: Monotonic transport cost reduction under rectification. Unique theoretical result.

summary: Flow Matching and Rectified Flow are a textbook parallel rediscovery, submitted within one month of each other (September vs October 2022) and both accepted to ICLR 2023. The core training objective is mathematically identical: regress a neural velocity field onto the direction (x_1 - x_0) along the straight-line interpolation x_t = (1-t)x_0 + tx_1 between noise x_0 and data x_1. Both recognize that this produces straighter ODE trajectories than diffusion models, enabling fewer sampling steps. The papers differ in emphasis and unique contributions: Flow Matching provides a more general theoretical framework (conditional flow matching for arbitrary probability paths, gradient equivalence theorem, connection to optimal transport); Rectified Flow provides the rectification/reflow procedure for iteratively straightening trajectories, distillation to one-step generation, and image-to-image transfer applications. The community has largely converged on 'flow matching' terminology while adopting the reflow/rectification ideas.
